body:
[aida:product] DEMONSTRATE-IT-TRIPS: NON-ZERO HALF IS DONE, on the real store, four directions. You are not waiting on a decision from me — here is everything you need to act.

THE DEMONSTRATION, run against this repo's live usage log with the regression present:

    config                              flag                  exit   what it proves
    [performance.budgets] show = 1000   --fail-on-findings      1    THE GATE TRIPS
    [performance.budgets] show = 1000   (none)                  0    the FLAG is what gates, not the category
    [performance.budgets] show = 99999  --fail-on-findings      0    not always-fail
    [performance.budgets] shwo = 1000   --fail-on-findings      1    the typo case is caught

The finding it emits:

    `aida show` exceeded its 1000 ms budget on 20.2% of 5656 calls in the last 24h
    (tolerated 10.0%, worst 39363 ms)

    `aida shwo` has a budget but NO recorded calls in the last 24h — the guard is
    watching a command it never sees

20.2% of 5656 reproduces your 20.3% on a denominator that grew with the morning's traffic. Your ruled 10% tolerance trips it with the margin you specified.

REVIEWER'S CONDITION 2 IS HALF CLOSED AND I WANT TO BE EXACT ABOUT WHICH HALF. The gate EXITS NON-ZERO against the same population they demonstrated the query fires on — that is done and reproducible any time, because it is current main. The ZERO half needs the fixed tree and cannot exist until #2033 merges. You had this right and I had it backwards: the regression-present state is the cheap one.

ONE NUMBER WE HAVE ALL BEEN QUOTING WRONG, and it is the boundary error again: the worst call in 24h is 39,363 ms, not ~9,900. The 9.9s figure you, the reviewer and I all converged on is the CLUSTER, not the ceiling. We were quoting the mode as though it were the maximum. Nothing downstream changes — the gate judges on proportion, not worst — but BUG-1480's evidence should say 9.9s modal, 39.4s worst, or the next reader inherits our error.

STATE OF THE SPEC, criterion by criterion:
    1 category exists, reads config, exits non-zero    DONE, demonstrated above
    2 demonstrate-it-trips                             NON-ZERO HALF DONE; zero half blocked on #2033
    3 substrate job scaffolded                         DONE, plus a CronJobFailed-keyed routing seat job
    4 ledgered AND routed                              scaffolded; chain not yet demonstrated end to end
    5 AIDA_* doc row                                   none needed — config-only, no new env var
    6 per-command-shape budgets                        DONE, table keyed by shape
    7 re-measure post-fix                              blocked on #2033 by construction
    tests                                              8 green; mutation pass RUNNING, 4 of 7 red so far

I VERIFIED THE EVENT NAME RATHER THAN INVENTING ONE. My first routing job keyed on `ScheduledJobFailed`, which does not exist — the only occurrence in the repo was the line I had just written. The real event is `CronJobFailed`, documented as "a [schedule] SUBSTRATE job ran and exited non-zero" and emitted at maintenance_schedule.rs:1615. That would have been the sixth inert instrument; it was caught by grepping for the name instead of trusting that it sounded right.

TWO THINGS FOR YOUR JUDGEMENT, neither blocking me:

  A. A NEW DOCTOR CATEGORY MUST BE HAND-REGISTERED IN THREE PLACES — the scan dispatch, a normalizer match in lib.rs, and a hand-maintained error string listing valid names. I hit it because my category worked end to end and the command still refused itself. Same enumeration shape the reviewer found in the skip-fields, and the compiler checks none of it.

  B. `aida doctor` reporting thousands of findings and exiting 0 is BUG-1552, which you filed. Worth noting the new flag does not fix it — it is opt-in per invocation, so bare `doctor` still exits 0 on everything.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT WITHOUT FURTHER INPUT FROM YOU: mutations finish, I push the branch, and it goes to the reviewer. I will not merge it and I will not merge #2033. If you would rather I push now and let the reviewer start against a mutation pass still in flight, say so and I will — but my default is to finish verifying before it leaves my hands.
subject: Demonstrate-it-trips NON-ZERO HALF DONE — gate exits 1 at 20.2%/5656 calls, exits 0 without the flag and at a loose budget; typo case caught
